# BLUETTI AC200L — my top recommendation

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="116px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station"/>**

    <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Sale price with code AFF5OFF (regular $899)</text>
    <badge color="success">Under $900</badge>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">2,048Wh · 2,400W · 30A RV outlet</text>
  </box>
</row>

Why I'd choose it:

- **RV-ready:** Built-in TT-30 30A RV outlet, so you can connect your RV shore-power cord directly.
- **LiFePO4 battery:** Long-life battery chemistry.
- **2,400W output:** Handles refrigerators, water pumps, lights, electronics and many kitchen appliances.
- **1,200W solar input:** Useful for off-grid camping.
- **Good sale price:** $854.05 with the supplied discount code.

Purchase: <Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="BLUETTI AC200L – $854.05 with AFF5OFF"/>.

The supplied results report it in stock on October 31, 2026. <Cite refs={["turn324359view0"]}/>

<Cite refs={["turn324359view0"]}/>

## Important RV considerations

There are two things I'd pay attention to before buying:

1. **30A outlet doesn't mean 30A of continuous power.** The AC200L's 2,400W inverter provides approximately 20A at 120V. It won't support the full 30A RV service or most rooftop air conditioners.
2. **Battery runtime:** A 2kWh battery doesn't necessarily last a full day. A refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker and other appliances can drain it quickly. Set a two-way refrigerator to propane when possible.

<Cite refs={["turn324359view0"]}/>

## My final verdict

- **Best RV-focused choice:** BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05.
- **Best value:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16.
- **Best for portability:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 at $899.99.

**One question that could change my recommendation:** 

Will you need to run your RV's rooftop air conditioner?

If yes, I'd reconsider the 2kWh category entirely, because a 2,400W portable station generally isn't sufficient for that job.
